clue.text: Evidently substandard establishment engaging with social worker?

indicators.note: something engaging another holds it within its grip, so the following pieces sit inside the first word

parts.note: the founding of a firm is its establishment
W is the standard abbreviation for with
the ant is the worker of a social insect colony

explanation.surface: A care home staffed by a social worker turns out to be below standard.
explanation.walkthrough: W and ANT together sit inside FOUND-ING. The 'with' of 'engaging with' does double duty in the surface, but here it is the abbreviation W.
explanation.definitionFit: To be found wanting is an idiom for being judged inadequate, so it describes something shown to be below par.

clue.text: Pipe of sorts, one of many introduced to cassoulet?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small high-pitched flute

definitions.text: one of many introduced to cassoulet
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a small pale bean, many of which go into a French bean stew

explanation.surface: A musical pipe somehow ends up in a French casserole.
explanation.walkthrough: Cassoulet is a slow-cooked French stew of beans and meats; the question mark flags that a bean, not an instrument, is what goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names both a small woodwind flute and a variety of green haricot bean used in stews.

clue.text: Join train heading north, having blown cover

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, so the word is turned back to front
losing its cover means the outer letters at each end are stripped away

parts.note: a train of attendants is a retinue

explanation.surface: A rail traveller links up with a train heading north after a secret agent's cover is blown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a railway train, but it is the retinue following a dignitary; reverse it to EUNITER and remove the first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to bring together or connect, a plain synonym of join.

clue.text: Finding not particularly "dancy" party

indicators.note: 'particularly' can mean 'very', so 'not particularly' asks for that intensifier to be removed

parts.note: a finding is a discovery
particularly means very, the part to drop

explanation.surface: A verdict that a party was not especially lively for dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around the invented adjective 'dancy' signal a party given over to dancing, which is fair as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a social gathering where people dance to recorded pop music, a dance-based party.

clue.text: Estate agent with higher voice that's posted overseas

indicators.note: in a down clue, higher means placed above, so this piece comes first in the column

parts.note: an air is a tune or melody for a voice
an estate agent who lets property is a letter

explanation.surface: An estate agent with a high-pitched voice is being sent abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' here is one who lets property, and 'higher' places the voice piece above it in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: An air letter is a lightweight sheet folded into its own envelope for sending by airmail abroad.

clue.text: Lots of compact event recording

parts.note: as in 'many times', a multiplied number of occasions
to tamp is to pack something down firmly

explanation.surface: Plenty of small vanity cases are logged at some occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compact' is the verb meaning press down, not the powder case.
explanation.definitionFit: A timestamp is a record of the date and time at which something happened, logging an event.

clue.text: East African guide quietly departs after noon

indicators.note: coming after puts the trimmed word behind the single letter in sequence

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for noon

indicators.note: whatever departs leaves the word, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: a pilot guides a ship into harbour
p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A local guide in East Africa slips away quietly once midday arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove P from PILOT and place N in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nilot is a member of the Nilotic peoples living around the Upper Nile in East Africa.

clue.text: Organised item at stops doddery old bubs periodically use?

definitions.text: Organised item at stops doddery old bubs periodically use?

indicators.note: something that stops a gap plugs it, so the first arrangement goes inside the second
something organised has been put into a new order, so the two words are rearranged
at regular intervals, so only every other letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
taken as written

indicators.note: a doddery walk is unsteady and wobbling, so the letters that follow are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An item fixed up at bus stops for the elderly 'bubs' to consult.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranged ITEM AT goes inside a mix of L, B, B and USE. The whole clue doubles as the definition: a printed schedule at the stop that elderly passengers check.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus timetable is the posted schedule of departures that passengers consult at stops, especially older travellers using free passes.

clue.text: Savoury rum's dispensed with a dash of relish by friend in estaminet?

indicators.note: what is dispensed with is done without, so a letter goes
a dash is only a tiny amount, pointing to the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: taken as written
the opening letter, the part removed
an estaminet is a small French cafe, where a friend is un ami

explanation.surface: A French cafe friend skips the rum and adds a little relish to something tasty.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove R from RUM, then add the French word for friend, hinted at by the French bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Umami is the fifth basic taste, the meaty savoury flavour found in broths and soy sauce.

clue.text: Did some eggs maybe get lost, 50 concealed in sack?

parts.note: scram is a curt order to go away

indicators.note: something concealed in another is tucked out of sight within it

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: Some eggs went missing, with fifty hidden in a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' looks like a bag, but it is slang for bed, which takes in the L.
explanation.definitionFit: To scramble eggs is to cook them beaten together in a pan, so the past tense covers cooking some eggs.

clue.text: The 90th Birthday racket-maker, say?

parts.note: one who makes a din, or racket
'for one' means for example, as 'say' does

explanation.surface: A noisy guest at a ninetieth birthday party, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the title of a famous comedy sketch, also called 'The 90th Birthday', shown every New Year's Eve in German-speaking and Scandinavian countries. DINNER is a jokey coinage for a maker of din.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinner for One is the British sketch, alternatively titled The 90th Birthday, where a butler serves Miss Sophie's imaginary guests.

clue.text: Official takes ball on as a result

parts.note: the ref is the match official
O is round like a ball
re means on the subject of

explanation.surface: A referee carries on with the ball as a consequence.
explanation.walkthrough: The official is THE REF, article included.
explanation.definitionFit: Therefore is the connective meaning for that reason or consequently, the same as 'as a result'.

clue.text: Can it be used for lingerie as well as gowns? It can

definitions.text: Can it be used for lingerie as well as gowns?

parts.note: 'it' is old slang for sex appeal, SA
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A question and its confident answer about a fabric suited to both underwear and evening dresses.
explanation.walkthrough: The question is the definition; the reply 'It can' is the wordplay, so the answer to the question is literally built from 'It' and 'can'.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a glossy smooth fabric widely used for both lingerie and evening gowns.

clue.text: Pub purchase exploits solicitor

parts.note: to milk a situation is to exploit it
a tout solicits custom, not a lawyer

explanation.surface: A lawyer takes advantage of someone in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' wants to be a British lawyer; here it is one who solicits business, a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk stout is a sweet dark beer brewed with lactose, an example of a drink bought at a bar.

clue.text: Nifty mover went and stole stone walls

indicators.note: walls enclose a space, so these letters go round the outside of the rest

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight
went is a euphemism for urinated
a boa is a feather or fur stole

explanation.surface: Someone quick on their feet left and stole a precious stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' is the scarf, not the verb, and 'went' is the bodily euphemism; 'stone' is the British weight of fourteen pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A speedboat is a fast motorboat, a nippy craft that moves quickly across water.

clue.text: Lost, naturally, without female

indicators.note: in its older sense without means outside, so the phrase wraps round the extra letter

parts.note: 'naturally' and 'of course' both mean obviously
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: Of course someone got lost, having no woman with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but it means outside, so the F goes in rather than out.
explanation.definitionFit: Off course describes a ship or traveller who has strayed from the intended route, so is lost.

clue.text: Use subterfuge to get old German viewpoint

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to fish for something by artful means
second meaning: a member of an ancient Germanic tribe that settled England
third meaning: a perspective or slant on something

explanation.surface: Trickery is needed to win over an elderly German's opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings of one word, not two; the Angles gave their name to England.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for scheming to obtain, a noun for a tribesman from Angeln, and a noun for a point of view.

clue.text: Folk might get a gander at these shows with episodes overladen with sentiment

definitions.text: Folk might get a gander at these

indicators.note: in a down clue, being overladen means having a load piled on top, so that piece comes first

parts.note: goo is sickly sentimentality
a series is a show broadcast in episodes

explanation.surface: Viewers sit through episodic TV dramas dripping with sentimentality.
explanation.walkthrough: A gander is a male goose, and also slang for a look; a farm where geese are kept is where folk would see one.
explanation.definitionFit: Gooseries are places where geese are bred, so visitors may spot a male goose there.

clue.text: This student band plays for debutante

indicators.note: the leftover letters play about, moving into a new order
'band plays for debutante' sets the word against the longer one, so the band's letters are cleared out of it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A student band performs at a society girl's coming-out ball.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike B, A, N, D from DEBUTANTE and rearrange the five letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutee is a pupil being taught by a tutor, a kind of student.

clue.text: Protect against combustibles whenever rolling back carpeting

indicators.note: rolling something back turns it in the opposite direction, so the word reads from its end

parts.note: if can mean whenever, as in 'if it rains, we stay in'
a carpeting is a telling-off

explanation.surface: Keeping flammables safe whenever a carpet is being rolled back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpeting' is the British slang for a reprimand, as when an employee is 'called on the carpet'.
explanation.definitionFit: To fireproof something is to treat it so it resists burning, guarding it from flames.

clue.text: Directors get on

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the body that runs a company
second meaning: to climb aboard a ship, train or plane

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests directors getting along; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a company's governing committee, and the verb means to embark on a vehicle.

clue.text: Further tip from attorney intercepts battle before court?

indicators.note: something that intercepts gets in the way between two points, so it goes inside

parts.note: the battle of Agincourt is AGIN placed before COURT

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its very point, the opening letter

parts.note: the tip, or first letter

explanation.surface: A lawyer's hint cuts across a fight that happens before the case reaches court.
explanation.walkthrough: Agincourt (1415) was Henry V's victory over the French, so the battle's name minus 'court' is what comes before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Again can mean moreover or besides, adding a further point to an argument.

clue.text: Driver must manage his surplus cattle

parts.note: over means left over, in surplus
a steer is a young bullock

explanation.surface: A cattle drover has to deal with an excess of livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driver' looks like a cattle drover, but it is a motorist, and the definition is a tendency a car can show.
explanation.definitionFit: Oversteer is a car turning more sharply than the driver intends, something the motorist must correct.

clue.text: Provide support for one's first wife after death

indicators.note: coming after puts these short pieces behind the opening word

parts.note: death is the end

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the word's opening letter
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Leaving money to one's first wife in a will after death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' selects the initial of 'one's'. The surface of a bequest fits the answer neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give a permanent income or fund, financially backing an institution or person.

clue.text: Thus, when taking booze half-heartedly?

indicators.note: half the heart goes, so one of the pair of central letters is removed

parts.note: so means thus
beer is booze

explanation.surface: This is what you stay if you drink only half-heartedly.
explanation.walkthrough: BEER has a double E at its heart; drop one. The whole clue then describes a light drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who drinks without enthusiasm stays sober, meaning not drunk.

clue.text: East to west, reputation precedes Mr Lancaster in love

indicators.note: precedes means goes before, so this piece comes first
a letter for the eastern direction travels from the right-hand end to the left of the word

parts.note: a good name is a reputation
Chris Lancaster is the Telegraph's crossword editor, so to its setters he is 'our Ed'

explanation.surface: A cryptic itinerary from east to west, with a reputation ahead of someone smitten.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the E of NAME from its right end to the front. Mr Lancaster is the puzzle editor of the paper that printed it, an in-joke many solvers found tough.
explanation.definitionFit: To be enamoured is to be captivated or infatuated, the state of being besotted.

clue.text: No Messiah: newborn in bothy has contrary manner!

indicators.note: something contrary goes the opposite way, so the letters for manner are read backwards

parts.note: a bairn is a Scottish child, apt for a bothy, a Scottish hut
an air is a manner, and those letters already sit in the middle of the child

explanation.surface: A baby in a highland hut is said to be awkward, not the Saviour.
explanation.walkthrough: The bothy points to a Scots word for child, whose middle three letters spell a manner; turn those round. The definition quotes Monty Python's Life of Brian: 'He's not the Messiah'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brian in Monty Python's film is mistaken for the Messiah, though his mother insists he is not.

clue.text: That is what's left from visiting Mars and Venus?

indicators.note: read as 'what has had left taken from it', so the abbreviation for left is removed from the phrase

parts.note: a trip to other planets is a visit to other worlds
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A space trip to two neighbouring planets, and whatever remains of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove L from IN OTHER WORLDS. 'That is' is the plain-English reading of i.e.
explanation.definitionFit: In other words and that is are both phrases introducing a restatement, like i.e.
